title: Change Nucleus software and contracts
summary: Modify Nucleus code, protocol, storage, Codex compatibility, authentication, service lifecycle, or deployment using the required guarded procedure.
use_when: Nucleus implementation, public protocol, persistent state, harness compatibility, authentication, service lifecycle, or deployment behavior is being changed.
do_not_use_when: The request is only to inspect or recover the installed runtime.
The change belongs entirely to Todo, Annals, Weaver, or another requester domain.
The user has not authorized release publication or deployment.
outcome: A minimal Nucleus change with the correct compatibility, execution-capacity, managed-authentication, migration, requester, documentation, CI, canary, and recovery obligations satisfied.
effects: Modifies Nucleus source, tests, contracts, or operator documentation.
Depending on the selected playbook, may require coordinated requester changes, database migration, exact Codex inspection, or service cutover.
Release and deployment remain separate externally consequential actions.
authority: Nucleus owns its protocol, store, adapter, global eight-slot scheduler, single-authority managed authentication broker, service packaging, and operator manual.
Requesters continue to own their domain contracts and must be changed only when the shared boundary requires it.
success: Every changed public or operational fact is reflected in the canonical operator manual and exact contract documentation.
The relevant generic and requester canaries prove the changed boundary after any deployment.
failure_and_recovery: Do not attempt binary-only rollback after an incompatible store migration.
Do not replace the proved Codex executable without adapter inspection and compatibility tests.

Preserve forward-only authentication separately from program or database rollback, including private staging and validated atomic promotion for every Codex credential-writing operation, supervised refresh and account reconciliation that survive requester cancellation, and attended-login exclusion from active job and account sessions.
privacy: Development fixtures, logs, and backups may contain complete prompts, model output, tool traffic, or credentials and must remain private.
Canaries create real runtime and sometimes requester-domain records; choose and account for them deliberately.
steps: Run `nucleus manual` and classify the change as a routine patch, protocol/client change, execution-capacity change, store migration, exact Codex upgrade, requester contract change, or authentication/service change.
Apply the smallest change in the owning Nucleus component and update all exact contracts and operator facts affected by it.
Run the Nucleus product CI and any affected requester CI suites.
If deployment is authorized, quiesce the required requesters, preserve the required recovery material, deploy in compatible order, and run layered canaries.
checkpoints: The primary authority and every cross-system obligation are identified.
Public compatibility, execution-capacity, authentication, and persistent-state consequences are explicit.
Deployment and publication have not occurred without separate authorization.
adaptation: Follow the exact playbook in the installed version-matched manual because store, harness, and requester compatibility facts evolve.
Use daemon-first or coordinated cutover ordering according to the compatibility shape actually introduced.
stop_when: A required migration or credential decision lacks safe recovery authority.
An affected requester cannot be quiesced for an incompatible operation.
The exact candidate Codex behavior has not been inspected and proved.
does_not_authorize: Running `release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Changing requester-owned domain meaning merely for runtime convenience.

consumers.statement: Nucleus maintainers may use this operation for an authorized change to Nucleus implementation, public protocol, storage, harness compatibility, authentication, service lifecycle, deployment behavior, or exact contracts.

preconditions.statement: The maintainer has read the installed Nucleus manual, identified the primary authority and every affected requester, and classified compatibility, execution-capacity, persistence, authentication, service, disclosure, migration, and recovery consequences.
Separate authority exists before release publication, installed deployment, a requester retry, a canary that creates durable records, or any destructive migration or credential move.

inputs.statement: Inputs are one authorized change request plus current Nucleus source, tests, runtime and operator contracts, affected requester contracts, installed harness evidence where relevant, and the applicable recovery playbook.
Requester-domain convenience, an unproved harness, an unsafe migration, or publication intent inferred from ordinary development is not a valid basis for changing Nucleus.

outputs.statement: The operation produces the smallest reviewed Nucleus source, test, and exact documentation change with scheduler and managed-authentication invariants explicit, the complete Nucleus product CI green, and affected requester proof synchronized.
Development completion alone does not publish a release, deploy the service, migrate live state, authenticate an account, retry requester work, or prove a production canary.

data_semantics.statement: Nucleus changes preserve the distinction between operational execution records and requester-owned domain truth, between public protocol and store schema, and between harness evidence and portable invocation semantics.
A green development candidate proves the checked-in contract and tests, while release, deployment, migration, and live canary outcomes remain separate externally consequential states.

identity_and_units.statement: Product release, public protocol version, store schema, adapter version, exact harness version, requester identity, entry contract version, and immutable schema or toolset identity are independently reviewed.
This development operation defines no runtime accounting or usage unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Completeness requires every affected source, test, requester, public and operator contract, execution-capacity invariant, managed-authentication boundary, migration, packaging boundary, recovery path, and focused canary obligation to agree before the product gate passes.
Exact Codex changes use freshly inspected executable, model-catalog, and generated app-server schema evidence rather than an assumed version range.
No development duration, release cadence, requester upgrade window, or review turnaround objective is promised.

access.statement: The operation uses the authorized local Nucleus source tree and shell surfaces; sensitive fixtures, backups, logs, credentials, canary records, and retained output stay within their documented private boundaries.
The operation grants no implicit access to requester-owned domain state, production credentials, external publication, installed service mutation, or private source disclosure.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The sequence is classify the change, name authorities and affected requesters, make the smallest owning edit, synchronize contracts and migrations, run Nucleus and affected requester gates, then separately authorize and perform any release or deployment.

Additive protocol support deploys daemon-first; incompatible changes retain both forms where possible or quiesce affected requesters, and store or credential recovery follows the exact guarded manual rather than binary-only rollback.

The supported capacity contract permits at most eight active attempts globally, leaves admitted overflow accepted with a pending attempt, counts waiting-on-requester as active, and starts each invocation timeout only after slot acquisition; it adds no workflow or retry authority.

Managed authentication permits account reads to overlap jobs while Nucleus serializes canonical credential operations, lets started refresh and account reconciliation settle after requester cancellation, and excludes attended login until active job and account sessions have ended. Every Codex credential-writing process uses private staging and only a validated atomic promotion advances the one authoritative credential.

operational_limits.statement: Stop when a destructive migration or credential move lacks safe recovery, an affected requester cannot be quiesced, exact harness behavior is unproved, or the proposed change would transfer requester-domain authority to Nucleus.
This operation cannot treat release.sh as a build step, bypass the complete product gate, silently change requester meaning, or use binary rollback across an incompatible store migration.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Changed public meaning advances the relevant protocol, schema, toolset, adapter, or capability-contract identity and retains supported historical decoding or supplies an explicit migration.
Deployment order and rollback are selected from the current version-matched manual according to the actual compatibility shape rather than source-workspace lockstep.
No universal backward-compatibility horizon, deprecation window, or release frequency is promised.

reliances.statement: Nucleus development relies on its registered Semantics repository for maintained project terminology while source, tests, and product documentation remain authoritative for behavior.
The documentation dependency on nucleus.execution.operate is not reinterpreted as a product runtime reliance of the source-change operation.
